{
  "IP": "neorv32_trng",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Generated random samples",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "Random bytes generated by the TRNG and queued for software reads; the IP's random-number service depends on their availability and value. They have no entering unit port because they are generated internally, and leave through the bus response data.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Confidentiality is at risk because generated random data is returned on bus_rsp_o.data at line 117; integrity is at risk because bus-controlled enable, clear, and pop operations can discard or alter which generated sample is delivered at lines 105-106 and 170-171; availability is at risk because disabling generation or clearing and consuming the FIFO can withhold samples through lines 137, 157, 165, and 170-171.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could issue bus writes and reads that disable generation, clear queued samples, or drain the FIFO, while observing the random values returned on the bus.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        360,
        366
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        117
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "TRNG enable setting",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The run-enable setting controls whether the internal generator operates and whether the FIFO is cleared. The setting is written through the bus and read back through the bus response.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data directly changes the stored enable setting at line 105; availability is at risk because the setting drives the generator enable at line 137 and participates in FIFO clearing at line 170, so changing it can stop random-data production.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could write a zero or otherwise unauthorized value to the enable control through the bus and disable random-data generation.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        105
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        95,
        105
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        109
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "FIFO clear command",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "A bus-written command requests clearing of the random-data FIFO, discarding queued samples. It is an internal control command with no direct output port.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data sets fifo_clr at line 106 and that command drives the FIFO clear path at lines 157 and 170, allowing queued random samples to be discarded; availability is at risk because the same clear operation can remove all pending data and interrupt required reads at lines 157 and 170.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could write the FIFO-clear control bit repeatedly to erase queued random samples and cause subsequent reads to lack data.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        106
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        94,
        101,
        106
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Random-data FIFO pop control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The internal read/pop decision determines when a bus data read consumes a random byte from the FIFO. It is decoded from the bus access but is not itself a bus port value.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because bus request strobe, direction, and address conditions generate fifo.re at line 171 and drive the FIFO read input at line 165, allowing the queued sample sequence to be consumed incorrectly; availability is at risk because altered pop commands can drain or fail to advance the FIFO and disrupt required random-data reads.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could issue crafted data-read requests to consume random samples at unintended times or repeatedly drain the FIFO.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        171
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C5",
      "Concept Name": "Random-data availability status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The FIFO's availability state indicates whether a generated random byte is queued and decides whether a read returns the queued byte or zero. It is generated inside the FIFO and leaves as a status bit in the bus response.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because FIFO clear and read operations alter the state producing fifo.avail at lines 157, 165, and 170-171, while the unit reports that state at line 112; availability is at risk because fifo.avail gates whether random data is returned at line 114 and can be made unavailable by clearing or disabling the FIFO at line 170.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could clear or consume the FIFO so that the availability status reports no sample and the bus returns zero instead of random data.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        167
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        112
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C6",
      "Concept Name": "Random-word valid indication",
      "Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Information": "The generator's valid indication marks completion of a random word and controls whether that word is written into the FIFO. It is an internal inter-block control with no direct unit boundary port.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because valid_o is produced from the sampling count at line 367 and drives the FIFO write enable through lines 138 and 162, so an incorrect indication can accept or omit a word; availability is at risk because withholding the indication prevents generated words from entering the FIFO at lines 138 and 162.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could perturb the generator's enable or sampling control so that the valid indication is withheld or asserted at the wrong time, causing missing or invalid FIFO entries.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        367
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO-buffered copy of generated random data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command fields as a separate asset",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The bus request record's access fields are command information folded into the settings and FIFO-control decisions, while the bus handshake is a transaction carrier rather than a separate piece of information."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response acknowledge and error status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error field is tied to a constant, so the bus-handshake-copy and constant-status rules leave no independent security asset."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO half-full and free-space status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "fifo.half and fifo.free are only wired from the FIFO and are not read, returned, or used to control another element in this unit, so no security objective and mechanism are shown."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "TRNG sequencing and debiasing state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The sample counter, debias state, and intermediate registers only sequence or shape production of the random result, so the sequencing-state and working-value rules do not make them independent information."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FIFO depth configuration",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "TRNG_FIFO fixes the FIFO build-time depth at lines 22 and 147, and no runtime element can change or withhold that value."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Simulation-mode setting",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "SIM_MODE and is_simulation_c are build-time values used at lines 111, 132, and 288, so they are not runtime conceptual assets."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset distribution",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_trng",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clock and reset inputs only time, reset, or distribute the generator and FIFO, which the clocks-and-resets rule excludes from conceptual assets."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: Random bytes generated by the TRNG and queued for software reads; the IP's random-number service depends on their availability and value. They have no entering unit port because they are generated internally, and leave through the bus response data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because generated random data is returned on bus_rsp_o.data at line 117; integrity is at risk because bus-controlled enable, clear, and pop operations can discard or alter which generated sample is delivered at lines 105-106 and 170-171; availability is at risk because disabling generation or clearing and consuming the FIFO can withhold samples through lines 137, 157, 165, and 170-171.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue bus writes and reads that disable generation, clear queued samples, or drain the FIFO, while observing the random values returned on the bus.

conceptual assets.information: The run-enable setting controls whether the internal generator operates and whether the FIFO is cleared. The setting is written through the bus and read back through the bus response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data directly changes the stored enable setting at line 105; availability is at risk because the setting drives the generator enable at line 137 and participates in FIFO clearing at line 170, so changing it can stop random-data production.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a zero or otherwise unauthorized value to the enable control through the bus and disable random-data generation.

conceptual assets.information: A bus-written command requests clearing of the random-data FIFO, discarding queued samples. It is an internal control command with no direct output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data sets fifo_clr at line 106 and that command drives the FIFO clear path at lines 157 and 170, allowing queued random samples to be discarded; availability is at risk because the same clear operation can remove all pending data and interrupt required reads at lines 157 and 170.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write the FIFO-clear control bit repeatedly to erase queued random samples and cause subsequent reads to lack data.

conceptual assets.information: The internal read/pop decision determines when a bus data read consumes a random byte from the FIFO. It is decoded from the bus access but is not itself a bus port value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus request strobe, direction, and address conditions generate fifo.re at line 171 and drive the FIFO read input at line 165, allowing the queued sample sequence to be consumed incorrectly; availability is at risk because altered pop commands can drain or fail to advance the FIFO and disrupt required random-data reads.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue crafted data-read requests to consume random samples at unintended times or repeatedly drain the FIFO.

conceptual assets.information: The FIFO's availability state indicates whether a generated random byte is queued and decides whether a read returns the queued byte or zero. It is generated inside the FIFO and leaves as a status bit in the bus response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because FIFO clear and read operations alter the state producing fifo.avail at lines 157, 165, and 170-171, while the unit reports that state at line 112; availability is at risk because fifo.avail gates whether random data is returned at line 114 and can be made unavailable by clearing or disabling the FIFO at line 170.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could clear or consume the FIFO so that the availability status reports no sample and the bus returns zero instead of random data.

conceptual assets.information: The generator's valid indication marks completion of a random word and controls whether that word is written into the FIFO. It is an internal inter-block control with no direct unit boundary port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because valid_o is produced from the sampling count at line 367 and drives the FIFO write enable through lines 138 and 162, so an incorrect indication can accept or omit a word; availability is at risk because withholding the indication prevents generated words from entering the FIFO at lines 138 and 162.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could perturb the generator's enable or sampling control so that the valid indication is withheld or asserted at the wrong time, causing missing or invalid FIFO entries.
